title: Top of Italy, pointless in Europe — Shakhtar on Wednesday
description: Lazio's 3–0 win at Juventus has drawn them level with Inter at the top, and Inter Women beat Parma 3–0 without conceding again.
mast_alt: Nerazzurri Daily Edition No. 48, Monday, October 19, 2026 — Top of Italy, pointless in Europe — Shakhtar on Wednesday

blocks.html: Inter lead Serie A with nineteen points and have none at all in the Champions League. They sit 29th of 36 teams in Europe, and Shakhtar Donetsk come to San Siro on Wednesday. Lazio are level with them at the top after winning 3–0 at Juventus, and Monday's papers all ask the same question about Europe.

blocks.h3: Inter have no points in Europe before Shakhtar visit
paras: Inter have no points from two Champions League matches and sit 29th of 36 teams. They lost 2–1 at Real Madrid and then 4–3 at home to Club Brugge.

The club's matchday calendar has Cristian Chivu, Inter's head coach, speaking at Appiano Gentile, Inter's training ground, at 8:30 AM ET on Tuesday (14:30 CEST). Kickoff on Wednesday is 3:00 PM ET (21:00 CEST).

blocks.h3: The club times the comeback at Bologna to the second
paras: Inter's own account of the match picks out the equalizer by Marcus Thuram, a center forward, in the 44th minute. It was a header from a cross by Nicolò Barella, a midfielder, and his fourth league goal of the season.
It also has Carlos Augusto, a left back, touching the ball 49 seconds after coming on. He scored in the 69th minute and crossed for Ange-Yoan Bonny, a center forward, to finish in the 83rd.

blocks.h3: Inter Women win again and have still not conceded
paras: Inter Women beat Parma 3–0 at the Arena Civica on Sunday. Haley Bugeja scored in the 39th minute, Karòlina Lea Vilhjálmsdóttir in the 58th and Michela Cambiaghi in the 87th.
That is three wins from three, nine points, eight goals scored and none conceded. The side coached by David Sassarini, Inter Women's head coach, is away at Napoli on Saturday.

blocks.h3: Gazzetta expects Provedel to make his Inter debut
paras: La Gazzetta dello Sport, Italy's biggest sports daily, expects Ivan Provedel, a goalkeeper who has not played a match since March 4, to start on Wednesday, with Josep Martínez rested. The paper says the change "non risponde a criteri meritocratici" — it is not a decision made on merit — but a chance to look at the new goalkeeper.
The same report has Hakan Çalhanoğlu and Andy Diouf, both midfielders, returning after resting at Bologna, and Bonny starting for the first time this season.
blocks.kicker: GAZZETTA DELLO SPORT VIA FCINTER1908 · OCT 19

blocks.h3: Sky and Corriere say Chivu raised his voice at halftime
paras: Sky Sport Italia reported on Sunday that Chivu was angry in the dressing room at halftime in Bologna, with the match level at 1–1. Corriere dello Sport carried the same account the same day.
Both say Inter had been second to Bologna's counterattacks for most of the first half. Corriere dello Sport adds that Thuram was booked for simulation in an incident Inter believed was a penalty.
